subject: general
question: By how much did urban infrastructure investments increase from Fiscal Year 2019 to Fiscal Year 2023?
solution:
The correct answer is __**10%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Urban infrastructure investments increased by 10% from Fiscal Year 2019 to Fiscal Year 2023.
 
• **This minor increase highlights a slower growth trend** in infrastructure spending during the specified period.
 
• **Urban infrastructure includes investments in transportation, housing, sanitation, water supply, and energy systems** that support urban areas.
 
• **The fiscal years are calculated based on the Indian government’s financial year, which runs from April 1 to March 31**.
 
• **The percentage increase reflects government policy priorities during this timeframe and economic factors impacting public spending.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Urban Infrastructure Terminology**: 

 
 
• **Urban infrastructure refers to the physical systems and facilities required for cities to function effectively, including roads, bridges, schools, and hospitals.**
 
• **It also encompasses services such as electricity, water supply, and waste management.**
 
 ** **
 
• **Government Investment Trends**: 
 
 
• **Investment trends in urban infrastructure are often influenced by economic growth, political priorities, and international funding agencies**.
 
• **Slower growth in investment can indicate economic constraints or shifts in policy focus to other sectors.**
 
 ** **
 
• **Fiscal Year Concept**: 
 
 
• **The fiscal year is a 12-month period used by governments and organizations for budgeting and financial reporting.**
 
• **In India, the fiscal year starts on April 1 and ends on March 31 of the following year.**
 
 ** **
 
• **Urbanization Challenges**: 
 
 
• **Rapid urbanization poses challenges such as congestion, pollution, and inadequate infrastructure**.
 
• **Investments in urban infrastructure are critical for sustainable growth and improving the quality of life in cities.**
 
 ** **
